persistOnly.why: 3 live writers (CreateVerticalCirculationCommand + residential generators); lifts are NOT serialized into the snapshot at all, so the rebuild cannot reconstruct base/top level refs — named by the rebuild's unreconstructable set. The last survivor of C71 §5.4's five prose families.

Written by PhysicsEngine (room → `physics-result-<roomId>`). The target is not an element and appears in NO snapshot slice — the measurement itself lives in the edge's metadata — so there is no authoritative state to reconstruct it from. It REMAINS persist-only and correctly stays on this ledger; what changed on 2026-08-17 is that the loss is now NAMED at load (§GR07-MEASUREDAT-NAMED), so it is no longer SILENT. A best-effort recompute does re-derive it after load (initDataPlatform enqueues every room on pryzm-project-loaded), but three silent early-returns guard that chain, so it is NOT declared REGENERATED.

struck.paidBy: §GR07-DECIDEDBY-REBUILD — the finding's own stated fix was WRONG, and the measurement overturned it. This ledger said to push 'decidedBy' onto `unreconstructable`; measuring first showed the loss was never real. `decisionRecords` (SerializedDecisionRecords) is persisted verbatim by BOTH ProjectSerializers, back-filled for older snapshots by MigrationEngine, and every DecisionRecord carries `elementId` authoritatively — so the rebuild now RECONSTRUCTS element → record.id, mirroring the IntentPrompt writer's direction exactly. Naming it as lost would have been the `contains` mistake repeated: a stale loss claim over a family whose source rides in the same snapshot. The family therefore also LEAVES the persistOnly ledger above — it is now regenerated-by-loader, not persist-only.
struck.provenBy: packages/persistence-client/__tests__/rebuildSemanticGraph.test.ts — two executed cases: the edge is rebuilt in both directions asserted by getTargets, a record with no elementId contributes nothing, and a snapshot with NO decisionRecords slice writes no edges and does not throw (edge count still pinned at 22).
